newsitem.title: USA: Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac pass capital test.
newsitem.headline: Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac pass capital test.

text.p: Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac were adequately capitalized as of the end of 1996, according to Office of Federal Housing Enterprise Oversight.

Core capital at Federal National Mortgage Association of $12.8 billion exceeded its minimum requirement of $11.5 billion under the Federal Housing Enterprises Financial Safety Act of 1992, the agency reported on Thursday.
Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp's core capital of $6.7 billion exceeded its minimum requirement of $6.5 billion.
Core capital included common stock, perpetual noncumulative preferred stock, paid-in capital and retained earnings.
